IBR-FaultScreen demo: IEEE 39-bus, 5,000 fault scenarios

Case: ieee39 · 5000 scenarios · Criteria: built-in PRC-029-1 file (illustrative non-standard limits)

IBR-FaultScreen v0.2.0
demo

Screening tool. It ranks contingencies for detailed study and does not replace an interconnection study. Demo on the IEEE 39-bus test system with generic IBR parameters and illustrative angle, recovery and frequency limits. Not a real system.
Dataset (version 2.0 with this demo; the link opens the latest): doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23290449 · Software: doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23290219

Network map

Each bus is shaded by the share of faults at that bus that were RISKY. Squares are generator buses; a teal outline marks an IBR's high-side bus in at least one scenario; a pulsing ring marks buses where at least 60% of faults were RISKY. Click or tap a bus for details. Press Play to watch risk grow as more synchronous machines are replaced by IBRs.

Select a bus to see its results.

0–20%20–40%40–60%60–80%80–100%no faults sampledgenerator busIBR high-side bustransformer

Bus positions follow the usual one-line drawing of this test system; they are not geographic.

Build your own grid

Pick which synchronous generators become IBRs (solar), where the three-phase fault happens and how fast it is cleared. Every combination here was simulated in advance with IBR-FaultScreen: 256 IBR sets × 29 fault buses × 5 clearing times = 37,120 runs on the IEEE 39-bus system at base load. The map colors every fault bus by its result for your choice; tap a bus to see why. The "screen view" on each case uses a screening model trained without that fault bus (the list of solver-hard buses that are always simulated comes from the whole training dataset).

IBRs replace
Clearing time

OK RISKY RISKY (bolted run unsolvable, milder fault RISKY) unknown (solver could not decide) IBR synchronous generator

Generic WECC IBR models and illustrative limits on a test system; screening only. "Unknown" means ANDES could not solve the bolted fault and the milder-fault check could not decide: such cases need a detailed study.

Quiz: guess first

Each question is a real simulated case from the explorer. Decide whether it is RISKY or OK, then see what the simulation found and what the screening model (which never saw that fault bus) would have guessed. The model is tuned to miss as few RISKY cases as possible, so it raises false alarms on purpose.

Model card

# Model card: IBR-FaultScreen screening classifier

- Model: `gbm`; decision threshold 0.03826 on P(RISKY)
- Trained on 4572 scenarios (1369 RISKY); dataset SHA-256 `e1b871d044603c9d315d9e08b74bdb5aef9a310a737963e8c465ebe1a2fa16a7`
- Versions: ibr-faultscreen 0.2.0, scikit-learn 1.9.1

## Intended use

Rank many fault scenarios so the riskiest are simulated and studied first. Every RISKY result shown to users is re-simulated (screen-then-verify). Not for use without simulation, and not a substitute for an interconnection study.

P(RISKY) is a ranking score, not a calibrated probability: the models are trained with class balancing and the threshold is set for recall, so a low threshold is expected. The calibration bins are in `evaluation.json`.

## Evaluation (honest)

GroupKFold by fault bus, 5 folds (nested). Recall target on RISKY: 0.95. Threshold tuned inside each training fold. AP = average precision.
Scenarios left out because their outcome is unknown: 428.

| Model | Recall | Precision | AUC | AP | Brier | Share flagged | TP/FP/FN/TN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rule | 0.95 | 0.46 | 0.784 | 0.524 | 0.306 | 0.62 | 1300/1522/69/1681 |
| logistic | 0.94 | 0.38 | 0.793 | 0.567 | 0.186 | 0.74 | 1288/2098/81/1105 |
| gbm | 0.96 | 0.48 | 0.863 | 0.674 | 0.161 | 0.60 | 1310/1441/59/1762 |

Model check (recall near the target and better ranking than the simple rule, on unseen fault locations): PASS. gbm: recall 0.96, precision 0.48, AUC 0.863, AP 0.674 | rule: recall 0.95, precision 0.46, AUC 0.784, AP 0.524

Extrapolation (train n_ibr <= 2, test n_ibr > 2):

| Model | Recall | Precision | AUC |
|---|---|---|---|
| rule | 0.85 | 0.51 | 0.689 |
| logistic | 0.99 | 0.42 | 0.696 |
| gbm | 0.99 | 0.48 | 0.816 |

### Study effort

Share of scenarios the `gbm` model sends to simulation for each recall target (held-out fault locations). The rest are passed without simulation.

| Recall target | Recall reached | Share flagged |
|---|---|---|
| 0.90 | 0.912 | 0.52 |
| 0.95 | 0.957 | 0.60 |
| 0.99 | 0.990 | 0.74 |

### Scenarios with an unknown outcome

Of 428 scenarios the solver could not settle (left out of training), the model alone would send 74% to simulation. Whether the solver fails depends mostly on the fault location, so the screen always verifies scenarios at solver-hard fault buses (below).

### Solver-hard fault buses

Buses where at least 20% of the dataset's scenarios ended with an unknown outcome. `screen` always simulates scenarios at these buses and at buses not in the dataset.

| Fault bus | Scenarios | Unknown outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 19 | 172 | 64 (37%) |
| 16 | 173 | 62 (36%) |
| 6 | 172 | 61 (35%) |
| 25 | 173 | 50 (29%) |
| 26 | 173 | 37 (21%) |

## What drives the predictions

Permutation importance (drop in AUC on held-out fault locations):

| Feature | Importance | Std |
|---|---|---|
| `clear_time_s` | 0.215 | 0.033 |
| `fault_v_pre_pu` | 0.045 | 0.020 |
| `z_fault_ibr_min_pu` | 0.044 | 0.015 |
| `scr_min` | 0.042 | 0.019 |
| `ibr_share` | 0.033 | 0.008 |
| `z_fault_gen_min_pu` | 0.014 | 0.012 |
| `fault_sc_mva` | 0.010 | 0.012 |
| `load_scale` | 0.010 | 0.008 |
| `inertia_h_s` | 0.009 | 0.002 |
| `ibr_mw` | 0.003 | 0.004 |
| `inertia_mws` | 0.001 | 0.002 |
| `total_load_mw` | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| `fault_x_pu` | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| `n_ibr` | -0.000 | 0.000 |

## Limits

- Learned from RMS simulations of one test system with generic IBR models.
- Fault locations never seen in training are the honest test; new networks are not covered until retrained on them.
- Labels inherit every limit of the criteria file and the dataset.

Limits

  • Screening only: it ranks contingencies for detailed study and does not replace an interconnection study.
  • RMS positive-sequence simulation (ANDES): no EMT effects, balanced faults only.
  • Generic WECC IBR models (REGCA1/REECA1/REPCA1), not a specific manufacturer.
  • Results depend on the criteria file; check its sources before relying on a verdict.
